vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: prompt-crafter
Version: 2.0.0

The skill bundle is an educational resource providing frameworks and examples for prompt engineering (RACE, Chain-of-Thought, etc.). It contains no executable code, system commands, or instructions to access sensitive data, and it explicitly includes safety guidelines for production use in SKILL.md.

llm.summary: The skill's content and requirements match its stated purpose (prompt-crafting) and it has no installs or credential requests, but a prompt-injection pattern was detected in the SKILL.md which could be used to override or manipulate agent instructions — review before use.

dimensions.detail: Name, description, and included examples align with a prompt-crafting skill. There are no unexpected binaries, installs, environment variables, or external endpoints requested — everything required is consistent with building and teaching prompt patterns.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md provides detailed prompt frameworks, chain-of-thought guidance, and many examples — all appropriate for the stated purpose. However, the static scan flagged a prompt-injection pattern ('ignore-previous-instructions') in the SKILL.md content. A phrase like this is not necessary for normal prompt-crafting teaching and could enable the skill (or prompts produced from it) to attempt to override prior or platform-level instructions. Inspect the file to find the exact occurrence and intent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files. This is low-risk from an installation/execution standpoint because nothing is written to disk or fetched at install time.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, credentials, or config paths. There is no apparent reason for any secret access based on the content.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not force-installed (always: false) and uses normal autonomous invocation defaults. It does not request persistent or cross-skill modifications. The main remaining concern is content that could encourage LLMs to ignore higher-level constraints if misused.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent for teaching and building prompts and doesn't request credentials or install code, but the SKILL.md contains or triggered a detection for an 'ignore previous instructions' pattern. Before installing or enabling autonomous use: 1) Open SKILL.md and search for phrases like 'ignore previous instructions' (or similar) — remove or rewrite any active templates that tell a model to ignore host/platform instructions. 2) If you plan to let the agent invoke the skill autonomously, test the skill in a sandboxed environment first so you can observe outputs without exposing accounts or data. 3) Do not provide any credentials to this skill (none are required). 4) If you want lower risk, use the SKILL.md as a local reference (copy/paste safe examples) rather than enabling the skill with autonomous invocation. If you can share the exact lines flagged, I can advise whether they are harmless (teaching about injection) or require edits.
llm.findings: [ignore-previous-instructions] unexpected: A pattern commonly used in prompt-injection attacks was detected in SKILL.md. While a prompt-crafting guide might discuss injection techniques to teach defenses, an actual occurrence of this pattern in examples or templates can be dangerous if an agent autonomously uses the templates. Verify whether the phrase appears as part of a defensive discussion or as an active template. If it's present in example prompts, consider removing or rewriting those examples.
